diff --git a/diagnose_duplicate_sources.py b/diagnose_duplicate_sources.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..3fb27e0a1d
--- /dev/null
+++ b/diagnose_duplicate_sources.py
@@ -0,0 +1,127 @@
+#
+# Gramps - a GTK+/GNOME based genealogy program
+#
+# Copyright (C) 2026
+#
+# This program is free software; you can redistribute it and/or modify
+# it under the terms of the GNU General Public License as published by
+# the Free Software Foundation; either version 2 of the License, or
+# (at your option) any later version.
+#
+# This program is distributed in the hope that it will be useful,
+# but WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without even the implied warranty of
+# MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.  See the
+# GNU General Public License for more details.
+#
+# You should have received a copy of the GNU General Public License
+# along with this program; if not, write to the Free Software
+# Foundation, Inc., 51 Franklin Street, Fifth Floor, Boston, MA 02110-1301 USA.
+#
+
+"""
+Diagnostic script: check whether a Gramps ID (e.g. S00032) appears more than
+once among the sources in a database.
+
+Usage:
+    python diagnose_duplicate_sources.py <database_directory> [gramps_id]
+
+Example:
+    python diagnose_duplicate_sources.py "C:/Users/Name/.gramps/grampsdb/familytree1" S00032
+
+If no gramps_id is given, the script lists every source whose gramps ID appears
+more than once.
+"""
+
+# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
+#
+# Standard Python modules
+#
+# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import sys
+
+# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
+#
+# Gramps modules
+#
+# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
+from gramps.gen.db.generic import DBMODE_R
+from gramps.gen.db.utils import make_database
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
+        description="Check for duplicate source Gramps IDs in a database."
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "dbdir",
+        help="Path to the Gramps family tree database directory.",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "gramps_id",
+        nargs="?",
+        default=None,
+        help="Specific Gramps ID to check (e.g. S00032). "
+        "If omitted, all duplicate IDs are reported.",
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    db = make_database("sqlite")
+    try:
+        # Open read-only so we don't need a write lock; this works even if
+        # Gramps has the database open.
+        db.load(args.dbdir, mode=DBMODE_R)
+    except Exception as exc:  # pylint: disable=broad-except
+        print(f"ERROR: could not open database '{args.dbdir}'")
+        print(f"  Exception type: {type(exc).__name__}")
+        print(f"  Exception repr: {exc!r}")
+        print(f"  Exception str:  {str(exc)!r}")
+        return 1
+
+    try:
+        handles = list(db.get_source_handles())
+    except Exception as exc:  # pylint: disable=broad-except
+        print(f"ERROR: could not read sources: {exc}")
+        db.close()
+        return 1
+
+    # Build a mapping: gramps_id -> list of (handle, title)
+    id_map: dict[str, list[tuple[str, str]]] = {}
+    for handle in handles:
+        source = db.get_source_from_handle(handle)
+        if source is None:
+            continue
+        gid = source.get_gramps_id()
+        title = source.get_title() or ""
+        id_map.setdefault(gid, []).append((handle, title))
+
+    if args.gramps_id:
+        # Report only the requested ID
+        entries = id_map.get(args.gramps_id, [])
+        if not entries:
+            print(f"Source {args.gramps_id} not found in the database.")
+        else:
+            print(f"Source {args.gramps_id} appears {len(entries)} time(s):")
+            for handle, title in entries:
+                print(f"  handle={handle}  title={title!r}")
+    else:
+        # Report all duplicate IDs
+        duplicates = {gid: ents for gid, ents in id_map.items() if len(ents) > 1}
+        if not duplicates:
+            print("No duplicate source Gramps IDs found.")
+        else:
+            print(f"Found {len(duplicates)} duplicate source Gramps ID(s):")
+            for gid in sorted(duplicates):
+                ents = duplicates[gid]
+                print(f"\n  {gid} appears {len(ents)} time(s):")
+                for handle, title in ents:
+                    print(f"    handle={handle}  title={title!r}")
+
+    db.close()
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

+## Overview
+
+The **GWizard Media Fix** tool helps genealogists clean up media files in a Gramps database.  It scans the database for missing files, duplicate references, and media stored outside the configured media base directory.  It can automatically rename files to a consistent naming convention, move scattered files into a single media folder, and generate a detailed report of any remaining issues.
+
+## Usage
+
+1. Open Gramps and select **Tools → GWizard Media Fix**.
+2. In the dialog that appears you will see a set of buttons:
+   - **Generate report** – creates a plain‑text report (`GWizardMediaFixReport.txt`).
+   - **Find missing media** – lists media records whose files are not present on disk and lets you supply a new path.
+   - **Fix media references** – resolves duplicate media records that point to the same file and removes unreferenced image tags.
+   - **Consolidate media location** – moves or copies all media files into the configured *Base media path* and applies the selected naming template.
+   - **Clean import notes** – removes stale “Records not imported into OBJE” notes after the missing files have been restored.
+   - **Accept all hints** – runs the three automated steps above in sequence, showing a preview of the changes before applying them.
+3. Follow the on‑screen instructions for each step.  Most actions present a preview table where you can edit the suggested new paths before clicking **Apply**.
+4. After applying changes, the tool updates the database and, where applicable, moves or copies the actual files on disk.
+
+## Configure Options
+
+* **Base media path** – the folder that Gramps uses for relative media paths.  Set this in *Edit → Preferences → Family Tree* or directly in the **Consolidate media location** dialog.
+* **Naming template** – choose one of the predefined filename templates or enter a custom pattern.  Tokens include:
+  - `{ref_id}` – reference ID (person, event, family, or media ID)
+  - `{surname}` – surname of the linked person (if any)
+  - `{given}` – given name of the linked person (if any)
+  - `{doc_type}` – description of the media
+  - `{year}` – year extracted from the event or person
+  - `{orig}` – original filename (used when *Keep original filename* is selected)
+  - `{hash}` – short content hash (optional for guaranteed uniqueness)
+* **Naming style** – *Use naming standard* (applies the chosen template) or *Keep original filename* (stores the file unchanged).
+* **File operation** – *Move files* (renames the original file) or *Make a copy* (leaves the original untouched).
+
+## Features
+
+* **Detect missing media** – finds media records whose files cannot be located on disk and suggests possible matches in the media base folder.
+* **Resolve duplicate references** – merges duplicate media records that share the same file, or creates separate copies for each reference.
+* **Consolidate media locations** – moves all media files into the configured base directory, applying a consistent, safe filename.
+* **Generate comprehensive report** – produces a human‑readable summary of all media issues, including missing files, permission problems, absolute paths, non‑standard filenames, duplicate references, and unreferenced files on disk.
+* **Automated “Accept all hints”** – runs the three main fix steps automatically, with a preview of the actions and a list of any items that still require manual attention.
+* **Clean stale import notes** – removes “Records not imported into OBJE” notes after the corresponding files have been restored.
+
+![GWizard Media Fix main dialog](images/gwizard_mediafix-main.png)
+
+![Find missing media dialog](images/gwizard_mediafix-find_missing.png)
+
+![Fix media references dialog](images/gwizard_mediafix-fix_references.png)
+
+![Consolidate media location dialog](images/gwizard_mediafix-consolidate.png)
+
+![Generated report preview](images/gwizard_mediafix-report.png)

+# Transcript: GEDCOM & Gramps Data Quality Standards
+
+## 1. GEDCOM Data Quality and Confidence Standard
+In the GEDCOM standard, data quality and confidence are officially designated by the **`QUAY` (Quality of Data)** tag. This tag represents a certainty assessment indicating the credibility of a piece of information based on its supporting evidence, typically attached to a source citation (`SOUR`).
+
+### The Standard Certainty Scale
+Across all major versions (including GEDCOM 5.5.1 and 7.0), the standard enforces a fixed, four-value numeric scale:
+
+| Code | Standard Meaning | Interpretation / Genealogical Context |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| **`0`** | **Unreliable** | Unreliable evidence, or data estimated from a random guess or suspect source. |
+| **`1`** | **Questionable** | Questionable reliability (e.g., formal/official text matched with a direct contradiction, or oral family traditions). |
+| **`2`** | **Secondary** | Secondary evidence, or data gleaned from an official document created a significant amount of time after the event. |
+| **`3`** | **Primary** | Direct, primary evidence, or data from an official document recorded at or very close to the time of the event. |
+
+### Limitations & Industry Reality
+* **Too Subjective:** The standard four-value system is considered too simplistic for serious evidence analysis.
+* **No "Direct vs. Indirect" Distinction:** The modern *Genealogy Proof Standard (GPS)* separates sources, information, and evidence into complex matrixes (Primary vs. Secondary sources; Direct vs. Indirect vs. Negative evidence). The basic `QUAY` tag cannot map cleanly to these.
+* **Inconsistent Software Support:** Many modern genealogy applications ignore it or use proprietary custom tags, which don't transfer perfectly between platforms.
+
+---
+
+## 2. Enhancing Value with Note Tags (`NOTE`)
+To implement a structured, machine-scannable rubric mirroring the GPS framework, you can standardize the data inside your plain-text notes.
+
+### Structured Tag-Value System Inside the Note
+```text
+[QUALITY ASSESSMENT]
+Source: [Original | Derivative | Authored]
+Information: [Primary | Secondary | Unknown]
+Evidence: [Direct | Indirect | Negative]
+Analysis: [Your brief textual explanation of why you gave it this rating]
+```
+
+### Definitions
+* **Source Type:** `Original` (first-hand material), `Derivative` (transcript/index), or `Authored` (compiled tree/book).
+* **Information Type:** `Primary` (provided by a firsthand witness close to the event) or `Secondary` (provided by someone not there or recorded long after).
+* **Evidence Type:** `Direct` (explicitly answers the question) or `Indirect` (requires combining clues to infer a fact).
+
+### GEDCOM Representation
+```text
+1 BIRT
+2 DATE 14 MAR 1882
+2 PLAC Boston, Suffolk, Massachusetts
+2 SOUR @S101@
+3 QUAY 2
+3 NOTE [QUALITY ASSESSMENT]
+4 CONT Source: Derivative (Online database index)
+4 CONT Information: Secondary (Birth date reported on a WW1 draft card decades later)
+4 CONT Evidence: Direct (Explicitly states a date of birth)
+4 CONT Analysis: The informant is the individual himself, which gives high confidence, but 
+4 CONT because this is an index of a record created 36 years after the birth, a primary birth 
+4 CONT certificate is still required to confirm.
+```
+
+---
+
+## 3. Gramps Genealogy Software Capabilities
+Gramps provides built-in, native features to categorize and track the quality, reliability, and confidence of a citation beyond plain-text notes.
+
+### 1. Built-in "Confidence" Menu
+Gramps features a built-in Confidence Dropdown Menu for citations. It internally handles a five-tier text scale that maps to GEDCOM standards:
+* `Very High` (Maps to GEDCOM Primary / 3)
+* `High`
+* `Normal` (Default fallback)
+* `Low`
+* `Very Low` (Maps to GEDCOM Unreliable / 0)
+
+### 2. Citation Attributes
+Every citation object in Gramps contains an **Attributes Tab**. Attributes are structured key-value pairs (Key, Value, and optional attached notes/sources). 
+* **Custom Customization:** Gramps has no built-in or pre-defined Citation Attributes out of the box. You must create your own keys (e.g., `Evidence Type`).
+* **Automation:** Gramps remembers your key history for auto-completion. You can also add blank fields to a citation template, move it to the **Gramps Clipboard**, and drag-and-drop it to duplicate fields rapidly across new citations.
+
+### 3. Color-Coded Tags
+Allows attaching custom colored labels to individual Citations for workflow signaling (e.g., Red for `Unverified / Guess`, Green for `GPS Certified`).
+
+---
+
+## 4. SuperTool Integration in Gramps
+The third-party addon **SuperTool** does not use or hardcode a standard mapping to Citation Attributes because Gramps doesn't define them natively. Instead, it provides Python proxy object accessibility.
+
+### Read Access
+SuperTool exposes an `attributes` list for citations evaluated as `(name, value)` string tuples:
+```python
+for name, val in citation.attributes:
+    if name == "Evidence Type":
+        print(val)
+```
+
+### Write Access / Automation
+To automatically create or modify custom tracking fields in bulk using SuperTool, you instantiate the core Gramps database libraries via its execution window using `SrcAttribute`:
+```python
+from gramps.gen.lib import SrcAttribute
+
+# Create a new attribute container
+gps_attr = SrcAttribute()
+gps_attr.set_type("Evidence Type")
+gps_attr.set_value("Direct")
+
+# Attach it to the citation being processed
+citation.add_attribute(gps_attr)
+```

+what kinds of sources are good examples in a GED file - is there more than one style?
+Good examples of sources in a GEDCOM file (.ged) are records that document an individual's life events with clear provenance, categorized primarily by reliability and type.
+
+Good Examples of Sources by Category
+
+• Primary / Original Sources (Created at or near the time of the event):
+	• Vital Records: Birth certificates, marriage licenses, and death certificates.
+	• Government & Legal Records: U.S. Federal Censuses (e.g., 1850–1950), land deeds, probate/wills, and military draft/service records.
+	• Church & Parish Records: Baptismal registers, church marriage ledgers, and burial logs.
+• Secondary / Derivative Sources (Created long after the event or compiled from other records):
+	• Published Works: Family histories, county history books, and local genealogies.
+	• Derived Documents: Delayed birth certificates, compiled memorial or obituary notices, and online user-submitted family trees.
+
+Is There More Than One Style?
+
+Yes. While a GEDCOM file stores data as plain text using standard tags (such as SOUR, TITL, AUTH, and PUBL), the citation style and formatting inside those source fields vary depending on the researcher or software:
+1. Evidence Explained (EE) Style:
+	• Created by Elizabeth Shown Mills, this is the gold standard and most popular framework in modern genealogy.
+	• It expands upon the Chicago Manual of Style to handle complex historical repositories, digital database images (e.g., Ancestry or FamilySearch collections), and microfilms.
+2. Chicago / Turabian Style:
+	• Frequently used in academic, historical, and traditional publishing contexts. Many genealogy programs build footnotes and bibliographies based on Chicago A/B variations.
+3. Short / Informal Free-Form Style:
+	• Many casual hobbyists or older software templates use a simple, non-standardized string (e.g., "1930 US Census, Chicago, Cook, IL, p. 4B") rather than a strict academic or archival template.
+4. Platform-Generated Style:
+	• Major platforms like FamilySearch or Ancestry auto-generate citations using built-in citation builders (often loosely adapted from Evidence Explained or proprietary formats), which sometimes drop specific church denominations, localities, or repository details.
+If you want, tell me which genealogy software or platform you are using (like Ancestry, RootsMagic, Gramps, or Family Tree Maker), and I can help you format your sources to match its best practices.

+I am using gramps
+
+In Gramps, managing sources is unique because the software uses a strict three-tier structural hierarchy rather than rigid, pre-baked text fields. Because Gramps doesn't force you into a specific academic citation style out of the box, you have the flexibility to format your records however you prefer.
+Understanding how to map your sources into the Gramps database structure and implementing popular formatting styles like Evidence Explained or Chicago Style can optimize your workflow.
+
+1. The Gramps Structural Hierarchy
+
+To make your sources clean and reusable, Gramps splits a historical record into three connected parts:
+ [ Repository ]  --> Where is it kept? (e.g., National Archives, FamilySearch website)
+       ↓
+   [ Source ]    --> What is the overall collection/book? (e.g., 1930 US Census, Smith Family Bible)
+       ↓
+  [ Citation ]   --> Where exactly is the piece of info? (e.g., Page 4B, Image 12, Entry #402)
+By organizing data this way, you only have to type the Source once, and you can create dozens of individual Citations that point back to it.
+
+2. Formatting Styles inside Gramps
+
+Since Gramps provides generic fields (like Title, Author, Publication info for Sources, and Volume/Page, Date, Confidence for Citations), you must choose a text style to fill them in. Two primary methods are widely adopted by Gramps users:
+
+Style A: "Evidence Explained" (The Split-Sourcing Method)
+
+This is the most popular method for serious genealogists because it treats major collections as single sources and leaves specific identifiers to the citation level.
+• Repository: FamilySearch or Ancestry.com
+• Source Title: United States Census, 1930
+• Source Publication Info: Washington, D.C.: National Archives and Records Administration, microfilm publication T626.
+• Citation Volume/Page: Illinois, Cook County, Chicago, Ward 12, Enumeration District (ED) 16-432, Sheet 4B, household 92, line 14, John Smith.
+• Citation Note: Paste the full transcription or the platform-generated permalink (ARK/URL).
+
+Style B: "Chicago / Traditional" (The Lumped-Sourcing Method)
+
+Common among users migrating from other platforms or those who run book-style reports. They prefer to put more descriptive text into the Source title itself.
+• Repository: Cook County Clerk's Office (Chicago, IL)
+• Source Title: Cook County, Illinois, Birth Certificates, 1871-1922
+• Source Author: Illinois. Cook County. County Clerk
+• Citation Volume/Page: Certificate No. 14205 (1895), Mary Higgins.
+
+3. Gramps-Specific Source Features to Utilize
+
+• Citation Format Preferences: Starting in recent updates (Gramps 5.2 and 6.0), you can go to Edit > Preferences to change your default Source/Citation handler. You can download "Enhanced Citation" or expert add-ons from the Gramps Plugin Manager to automatically pull Repository names directly into your generated reports.
+• Source/Citation Attributes: You can add custom key-value pairs (Attributes) to a citation. A great convention used by Gramps community members is creating a Quality or EvidenceType attribute to categorize whether a document provides Direct, Indirect, or Primary information.
+• Centralized Media: Instead of attaching images randomly, attach your digitized record images (like a scanned PDF of a marriage license) directly to the Citation object. This links the visual evidence to the specific text citation it proves.
+Would you like an exact step-by-step example of how to enter a specific record type (like an online census record or a physical family bible) using the Gramps interface?

+What do you do when you have a source with an actual picture of a birth or death certificate or headstone, marriage license, etc?
+
+When you have an actual digital image of a record, you want to link it so that anyone viewing your tree can instantly see the proof. In Gramps, the absolute best practice is to attach the image file directly to the Citation, not the person and not the overall Source.
+This ensures that the image is tied directly to the specific piece of data it extracts (e.g., the birth date or burial location), and keeps your database cleanly organized.
+
+The Workflow in Gramps
+
+
+1. Save and Name Your Image File (Outside of Gramps)
+
+Before importing the image, save it to a dedicated folder on your computer (e.g., Documents/Genealogy/Media). Give it a clean, descriptive file name so it is easy to search later.
+• Good Name: smith_john_birth_certificate_1920.jpg
+• Bad Name: IMG_4829.jpg
+
+2. Create the Hierarchy (Inside Gramps)
+
+1. Go to the Sources view and open or create the overarching Source (e.g., "Illinois Vital Records").
+2. Inside that Source, create a Citation for this specific person (e.g., “Birth Certificate #12345 for John Smith”).
+
+3. Attach the Image to the Citation
+
+1. Double-click to open your newly created Citation window.
+2. Click on the Gallery tab at the top of the Citation window.
+3. Click the + (Add) button. This will open the Media Reference Editor.
+4. Click the folder icon next to the Path field to browse your computer and select your image file.
+5. Gramps will prompt you to create a new Media Object. Give the media object a clean title (e.g., "John Smith Birth Certificate Image").
+6. Click OK to save.
+
+Where the Hierarchy Connects
+
+When you are finished, Gramps links your digital artifact cleanly down the chain:
+text
+ [ Person: John Smith ] 
+       ↓ (Linked to Birth Event)
+ [ Citation: Birth Certificate #12345 ]
+       ↳ 📂 Gallery Tab: [ smith_john_birth_certificate_1920.jpg ] 
+       ↓ (Points to)
+ [ Source: Illinois Vital Records ]
+Use code with caution.
+
+Pro-Tips for Handling Document Images in Gramps
+
+• Set the Attributes: Within the Media Reference Editor window, you can change the Attribute or Type of the image to Document, Tombstone, or Certificate. This helps Gramps categorize it properly when generating graphic reports or websites.
+• Transcribe it in the Notes: Do not just rely on the picture. Open the Notes tab inside that same Citation, create a new note, and type out an exact transcription of what the certificate or headstone says. This makes the text fully searchable within Gramps, which a picture file is not.

+
+In a GEDCOM file are source/citations associate with only events, or also individuals and families?
+
+In a GEDCOM file, source citations can be associated with events, individuals, and families alike.
+GEDCOM is a highly flexible format designed to let researchers document exactly where they found any piece of information. Because of this, citations can be linked at multiple levels of the file structure:
+• Individual Level (0 @I1@ INDI): You can attach a source to an entire person. This is typically used to cite a broad source—like a comprehensive biography or a specific family tree book—that validates the person's identity or overall existence.
+• Family Level (0 @F1@ FAM): You can link a source directly to a family record. This is often used for sources that prove the family structure or relationship as a whole, such as a census record showing parents and children living together.
+• Event Level: This is the most common use. You can attach a citation to specific events within an individual or family record, such as a birth (BIRT), marriage (MARR), or death (DEAT). For example, a birth certificate source would be attached directly to the birth event rather than the person as a whole.
+• Attribute Level: You can also attach sources to specific characteristics or attributes, such as a person's occupation (OCCU), physical description (DSCR), or religion (RELI).
+If you are working on a specific genealogy project, let me know:
+• Are you writing a program to parse a GEDCOM file, or manually cleaning up your tree?
+• Which genealogy software are you using to export or import the file?
+I can provide specific examples of the GEDCOM tag syntax if that would help.
+
+I am working with Gramps genealogy software.  In GEDCOM, is there a URL field which is associated with a source/citation reference?
+
+In the traditional and widely used GEDCOM 5.5 and 5.5.1 standards, there is no official, dedicated URL field directly inside a source citation reference.
+Because of this limitation in the GEDCOM specification, genealogy programs handle citation URLs using various structural workarounds.
+
+How Gramps Handles Citation URLs
+
+Gramps users frequently run into this issue when exporting their family trees. In the Gramps interface, the citation object traditionally lacks a designated "Internet/URL" field. Community consensus on Gramps Discourse shows three common workarounds to ensure URLs export properly into a GEDCOM file:
+1. The Volume/Page Field Appending Method (Most Common):
+Many users paste the direct permalink directly into the Volume/Page field, appending it right after the page number or location. When Gramps exports to GEDCOM, this data maps to the standard PAGE tag.gedcom
+3 PAGE Page 42, https://example.com
+Use code with caution.
+This is highly recommended if you are transferring data to websites like WikiTree, which parse strings inside the PAGE tag and automatically turn valid URLs into hotlinks.
+2. Attaching a Note to the Citation:
+You can create a text Note in Gramps, paste your URL inside it, and link that Note to your Citation. During export, Gramps generates a native GEDCOM NOTE block nested under the citation.gedcom
+2 SOUR @S1@
+3 PAGE Page 42
+3 NOTE https://example.com
+Use code with caution.
+The downside is that external software treats notes as separate entities, meaning the URL might display further down the page rather than beautifully inline with the citation text.
+3. Media Object Links:
+If the URL links to a concrete image or digital file, you can add it as a Media item attached to the citation, setting the path structure to an internet address.
+
+The Future: GEDCOM 7.0
+
+If you are planning workflows around modern genealogy tools, the GEDCOM 7.0 standard officially resolved this structural gap. It natively introduces the WWW tag, allowing software to associate web addresses directly with a specific citation structure without burying it inside page or text fields.
+If you want to streamline this, let me know:
+• Is your primary goal to manually clean up your data fields so they format beautifully inside Gramps?
+• Or are you prepping a GEDCOM export for a specific web platform (like WikiTree, Ancestry, or FamilySearch)?
+I can give you the quickest way to batch-manage or format these entries.

+
+Does gramps support gedcom 7.0?
+
+Gramps does not officially support GEDCOM 7.0 out of the box as a core feature, though full compatibility is a major ongoing objective.
+How GEDCOM 7.0 capability breaks down depends on the platform version:
+
+1. The Core Desktop Application (Gramps 6.0+)
+
+If you use the standard Gramps desktop application, it still uses GEDCOM 5.5.1 as its default standard for standard file imports and exports.
+• Partial 7.0 Features: Modern releases like Gramps 6.0 have slowly adopted specific GEDCOM 7.0 concepts. For example, it natively supports GEDCOM 7.0-styled association roles (like Neighbor, Officiator, and Friend) within the software.
+• The Structural Hurdle: Gramps and GEDCOM have fundamental data model differences. In Gramps, events are "first-class" independent objects that multiple people can share, whereas older GEDCOM files treat events strictly as attributes embedded under a single person. Gramps developers are actively working alongside FamilySearch on GEDCOM 7 extensions to finally resolve these gaps.
+
+2. The Community Workaround: gramps-gedcom7
+
+For desktop users needing immediate compatibility, there is a highly functional third-party Python library called gramps-gedcom7 on GitHub developed by David Straub.
+• Importing: It provides robust, tested, and reliable capability to import GEDCOM 7.0 files into a Gramps database.
+• Exporting: The export feature in this tool is newer and handles conversions well, though a few minor variables (like the registered researcher metadata) are still being refined.
+• Limitation: It functions primarily as a command-line tool or a Python script interface rather than a clickable, native "Addon" menu button inside the desktop program. However, a standalone web converter tool is provided where you can upload a GEDCOM 7 file and convert it into a native Gramps XML file to open smoothly in your database.
+
+3. Gramps Web Natively Supports It
+
+If you run Gramps Web (the collaborative web app ecosystem built for Gramps), GEDCOM 7.0 imports are natively supported! The platform has directly integrated the standalone library into its core backend, automatically detecting if an uploaded tree is a legacy version or a newer GEDCOM 7 file.
+If you are planning to handle a GEDCOM 7.0 file, let me know:
+• Do you need to import a 7.0 file into Gramps, or are you hoping to export out of Gramps in the 7.0 format?
+• Are you comfortable using a web converter tool, or do you strictly need a desktop solution?
+I can provide the step-by-step instructions to convert your data safely.

+== Overview ==
+
+The '''GWizard Media Fix''' tool helps genealogists clean up media files in a Gramps database.  It scans the database for missing files, duplicate references, and media stored outside the configured media base directory.  It can automatically rename files to a consistent naming convention, move scattered files into a single media folder, and generate a detailed report of any remaining issues.
+
+== Usage ==
+
+# Open Gramps and select '''Tools → GWizard Media Fix'''.
+# In the dialog that appears you will see a set of buttons:
+* '''Generate report''' – creates a plain‑text report (<code>GWizardMediaFixReport.txt</code>).
+* '''Find missing media''' – lists media records whose files are not present on disk and lets you supply a new path.
+* '''Fix media references''' – resolves duplicate media records that point to the same file and removes unreferenced image tags.
+* '''Consolidate media location''' – moves or copies all media files into the configured ''Base media path'' and applies the selected naming template.
+* '''Clean import notes''' – removes stale “Records not imported into OBJE” notes after the missing files have been restored.
+* '''Accept all hints''' – runs the three automated steps above in sequence, showing a preview of the changes before applying them.
+# Follow the on‑screen instructions for each step.  Most actions present a preview table where you can edit the suggested new paths before clicking '''Apply'''.
+# After applying changes, the tool updates the database and, where applicable, moves or copies the actual files on disk.
+
+== Configure Options ==
+
+'' '''Base media path''' – the folder that Gramps uses for relative media paths.  Set this in ''Edit → Preferences → Family Tree* or directly in the '''Consolidate media location''' dialog.
+* '''Naming template''' – choose one of the predefined filename templates or enter a custom pattern.  Tokens include:
+* <code>{ref_id}</code> – reference ID (person, event, family, or media ID)
+* <code>{surname}</code> – surname of the linked person (if any)
+* <code>{given}</code> – given name of the linked person (if any)
+* <code>{doc_type}</code> – description of the media
+* <code>{year}</code> – year extracted from the event or person
+* <code>{orig}</code> – original filename (used when ''Keep original filename'' is selected)
+* <code>{hash}</code> – short content hash (optional for guaranteed uniqueness)
+'' '''Naming style''' – ''Use naming standard'' (applies the chosen template) or ''Keep original filename* (stores the file unchanged).
+'' '''File operation''' – ''Move files'' (renames the original file) or ''Make a copy* (leaves the original untouched).
+
+== Features ==
+
+* '''Detect missing media''' – finds media records whose files cannot be located on disk and suggests possible matches in the media base folder.
+* '''Resolve duplicate references''' – merges duplicate media records that share the same file, or creates separate copies for each reference.
+* '''Consolidate media locations''' – moves all media files into the configured base directory, applying a consistent, safe filename.
+* '''Generate comprehensive report''' – produces a human‑readable summary of all media issues, including missing files, permission problems, absolute paths, non‑standard filenames, duplicate references, and unreferenced files on disk.
+* '''Automated “Accept all hints”''' – runs the three main fix steps automatically, with a preview of the actions and a list of any items that still require manual attention.
+* '''Clean stale import notes''' – removes “Records not imported into OBJE” notes after the corresponding files have been restored.
+

++def find_duplicate_media_groups(db: Any) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
++    """Scan database for media files referenced by multiple media records.
++
++    Returns a list of dicts describing each shared file and its referencing media records.
++    """
++    if not db:
++        return []
++
++    try:
++        from .gwizardmediafix import (
++            resolve_media_reference_context,
++            check_path_permission,
++        )
++    except (ImportError, ValueError):
++        from gwizardmediafix import (  # type: ignore[import-not-found,no-redef]
++            resolve_media_reference_context,
++            check_path_permission,
++        )
++
++    path_map: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = {}
++
++    for media in db.iter_media():
++        m_handle = str(media.get_handle() or "")
++        m_gid = str(media.get_gramps_id() or "")
++        desc = str(media.get_description() or "")
++        raw_path = clean_path(str(media.get_path() or ""))
++        if not raw_path:
++            continue
++
++        try:
++            full_path = media_path_full(db, raw_path)
++            key = os.path.normcase(os.path.normpath(full_path))
++        except Exception:
++            key = os.path.normcase(os.path.normpath(raw_path))
++
++        assoc_str = ""
++        try:
++            ctx = resolve_media_reference_context(db, media)
++            assoc_str = ctx.get("assoc", "")
++        except Exception:
++            pass
++
++        perm_issue, inaccess_dir = check_path_permission(full_path)
++        if not perm_issue and os.path.isabs(raw_path):
++            perm_issue, inaccess_dir = check_path_permission(raw_path)
++
++        backlinks = []
++        if hasattr(db, "find_backlink_handles") and m_handle:
++            try:
++                backlinks = list(db.find_backlink_handles(m_handle))
++            except Exception:
++                backlinks = []
++
++        if key not in path_map:
++            path_map[key] = []
++
++        path_map[key].append(
++            {
++                "handle": m_handle,
++                "gramps_id": m_gid,
++                "desc": desc,
++                "raw_path": raw_path,
++                "full_path": key,
++                "backlink_count": len(backlinks),
++                "assoc": assoc_str,
++                "perm_issue": perm_issue,
++                "inaccess_dir": inaccess_dir,
++                "media": media,
++            }
++        )
++
++    groups: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
++    # 1. Duplicate file references (multiple media records sharing the same file)
++    for file_key, records in path_map.items():
++        if len(records) > 1:
++            records.sort(
++                key=lambda r: (
++                    -r["backlink_count"],
++                    not r["assoc"],
++                    not r["desc"],
++                    r["gramps_id"],
++                )
++            )
++            keeper = records[0]
++            groups.append(
++                {
++                    "type": "duplicate",
++                    "file_key": file_key,
++                    "records": records,
++                    "keeper": keeper,
++                    "raw_path": records[0]["raw_path"],
++                    "perm_issue": any(r.get("perm_issue") for r in records),
++                    "inaccess_dir": next(
++                        (r["inaccess_dir"] for r in records if r.get("inaccess_dir")),
++                        None,
++                    ),
++                }
++            )
++
++    # 2. Unreferenced media records (image tags with 0 data references)
++    for records in path_map.values():
++        if len(records) == 1 and records[0]["backlink_count"] == 0:
++            r = records[0]
++            groups.append(
++                {
++                    "type": "unreferenced",
++                    "file_key": r["full_path"],
++                    "records": [r],
++                    "keeper": r,
++                    "raw_path": r["raw_path"],
++                    "perm_issue": r.get("perm_issue", False),
++                    "inaccess_dir": r.get("inaccess_dir"),
++                }
++            )
++
++    # 2. Unreferenced media records (image tags with 0 data references)
++    for records in path_map.values():
++        if len(records) == 1 and records[0]["backlink_count"] == 0:
++            r = records[0]
++            groups.append(
++                {
++                    "type": "unreferenced",
++                    "file_key": r["full_path"],
++                    "records": [r],
++                    "keeper": r,
++                    "raw_path": r["raw_path"],
++                    "perm_issue": r.get("perm_issue", False),
++                    "inaccess_dir": r.get("inaccess_dir"),
++                }
++            )
++
++    return groups
++

++            str(_("Hints accepted")),
++            str(
++                _(
++                    "Populated merge suggestions for %d shared media files. Review and press Apply."
++                )
++                % count
++            ),
++            parent=self,
++        )
++
++    def cb_apply(self, _button: Gtk.Button) -> None:
++        merged_count = 0
++        copied_count = 0
++        deleted_count = 0
++        errors: list[str] = []
++
++        for target in self.row_targets:
++            combo = target["action_combo"]
++            choice = 0
++            if hasattr(combo, "get_active"):
++                raw_choice = combo.get_active()
++                try:
++                    choice = int(raw_choice)
++                except (TypeError, ValueError):
++                    choice = 0
++            group = target["group"]
++            g_type = group.get("type", "duplicate")
++
++            if g_type == "unreferenced":
++                if choice == 0:
++                    h = group["keeper"]["handle"]
++                    try:
++                        with DbTxn(
++                            _("Remove Unreferenced Media"), self.dbstate.db
++                        ) as trans:
++                            self.dbstate.db.remove_media(h, trans)
++                            deleted_count += 1
++                    except Exception as err:
++                        LOG.exception("Failed to remove unreferenced media: %s", err)
++                        errors.append(str(err))
++                continue
++
++            if choice == 2:  # Keep shared (no change)
++                continue
++
++            records = group["records"]
++            keeper = group["keeper"]
++
++            if choice == 0:
++                # Merge duplicate records into keeper
++                keeper_media = self.dbstate.db.get_media_from_handle(keeper["handle"])
++                if not keeper_media:
++                    continue
++                for other in records:
++                    if other["handle"] == keeper["handle"]:
++                        continue
++                    try:
++                        other_media = self.dbstate.db.get_media_from_handle(
++                            other["handle"]
++                        )
++                        if other_media:
++                            query = MergeMediaQuery(
++                                self.dbstate, keeper_media, other_media
++                            )
++                            query.execute()
++                            merged_count += 1
++                    except Exception as err:
++                        LOG.exception("Failed to merge media record: %s", err)
++                        errors.append(str(err))
++
++            elif choice == 1:
++                # Create separate file copies for each duplicate record
++                src_path = clean_path(group["raw_path"])
++                try:
++                    src_full = clean_path(media_path_full(self.dbstate.db, src_path))
++                except Exception:
++                    src_full = src_path
++
++                base, ext = os.path.splitext(src_path)
++                claimed: set[str] = set()
++                with DbTxn(_("Split Media References"), self.dbstate.db) as trans:
++                    for r in records[1:]:
++                        new_rel = f"{base}_{r['gramps_id']}{ext}"
++                        try:
++                            expected = media_path_full(self.dbstate.db, new_rel)
++                        except Exception:
++                            expected = new_rel
++                        if not os.path.exists(src_full):
++                            errors.append(
++                                "[%s] source file not found: %s"
++                                % (r["gramps_id"], src_full)
++                            )
++                            continue
++                        dest_full = unique_destination(expected, claimed, src_full)
++                        if dest_full != expected:  # keep DB path and disk name in step
++                            extra = os.path.splitext(dest_full)[0][
++                                len(os.path.splitext(expected)[0]) :
++                            ]
++                            new_rel = f"{base}_{r['gramps_id']}{extra}{ext}"
++                        ok, err = relocate_file(src_full, dest_full, copy=True)
++                        if not ok:
++                            LOG.warning("Failed to copy media file: %s", err)
++                            errors.append("[%s] %s" % (r["gramps_id"], err))
++                            continue
++                        copied_count += 1
++                        other_media = self.dbstate.db.get_media_from_handle(r["handle"])
++                        if other_media:
++                            other_media.set_path(new_rel)
++                            self.dbstate.db.commit_media(other_media, trans)
++
++        if merged_count == 0 and copied_count == 0 and deleted_count == 0:
++            OkDialog(
++                str(_("Nothing to apply")),
++                str(
++                    _(
++                        "No actions selected. Choose 'Merge', 'Create copies', or 'Delete' for one or more records first."
++                    )
++                ),
++                parent=self,
++            )
++            return
++
++        summary = []
++        if merged_count > 0:
++            summary.append(str(_("Merged %d duplicate media records.")) % merged_count)
++        if copied_count > 0:
++            summary.append(str(_("Created %d separate media files.")) % copied_count)
++        if deleted_count > 0:
++            summary.append(
++                str(_("Deleted %d unreferenced media records.")) % deleted_count
++            )
++
++        msg = " ".join(summary)
++        if errors:
++            msg += "\n\n" + "\n".join(errors)
++        OkDialog(
++            str(_("Media References Resolved")),
++            msg + "\n\n" + str(_("Close and reopen this dialog to rescan.")),
++            parent=self,
++        )
++
++        # Update button sensitivities and group records after applying
++        self.groups = []
++        self.row_targets = []
++        if hasattr(self, "apply_button"):
++            self.apply_button.set_sensitive(False)
++        if hasattr(self, "accept_button"):
++            self.accept_button.set_sensitive(False)
++
++    def show_dialog(self) -> None:
++        self.show_all()
++        while True:
++            resp = self.run()
++            if resp in (
++                Gtk.ResponseType.CLOSE,
++                Gtk.ResponseType.CANCEL,
++                Gtk.ResponseType.DELETE_EVENT,
++            ):
++                break
++        self.destroy()

++class SelectableLabel(Gtk.Label):
++    """Gtk.Label subclass that is selectable, left-aligned, and wrappable by default."""
++
++    def __init__(
++        self,
++        label: str = "",
++        selectable: bool = True,
++        wrap: bool = True,
++        xalign: float = 0.0,
++        markup: bool = False,
++        can_focus: bool = False,
++        max_width_chars: int | None = None,
++        size_request: tuple[int, int] | None = None,
++        **kwargs: Any,
++    ) -> None:
++        """Initialize the selectable label with standard formatting defaults."""
++        super().__init__(**kwargs)
++        if markup:
++            self.set_markup(label)
++        else:
++            self.set_text(label)
++
++        self.set_selectable(selectable)
++        self.set_halign(Gtk.Align.START)
++        self.set_xalign(xalign)
++        self.set_can_focus(can_focus)
++
++        if wrap:
++            self.set_line_wrap(True)
++            self.set_line_wrap_mode(Pango.WrapMode.WORD_CHAR)
++
++        if max_width_chars is not None:
++            self.set_max_width_chars(max_width_chars)
++
++        if size_request is not None:
++            self.set_size_request(*size_request)

++# ------------------------------------------------------------
++#
++# Pure path helpers (no GTK / Gramps dependency; unit-testable)
++#
++# ------------------------------------------------------------
++def clean_path(path: str | None) -> str:
++    """Strip whitespace and surrounding quotes from a path string.
++
++    Matched pairs of quotes are removed.  An unmatched double quote is removed
++    (never valid in a Windows filename), but an unmatched apostrophe is kept
++    because it can legitimately end a folder name ("Grandma's").
++    """
++    if not path:
++        return ""
++    p = str(path).strip()
++    while len(p) >= 2 and p[0] == p[-1] and p[0] in "\"'":
++        p = p[1:-1].strip()
++    if p.startswith('"'):
++        p = p[1:].strip()
++    if p.endswith('"'):
++        p = p[:-1].strip()
++    return p
++
++
++def is_absolute_path(path: str | None) -> bool:
++    """Return True for drive-absolute AND rooted drive-less paths.
++
++    Python 3.13+ on Windows no longer treats "/Users/x" as absolute, but GEDCOM
++    imports commonly produce exactly such paths (drive letter stripped).  Treat
++    them as absolute so they are not mistaken for paths relative to the media
++    base directory.
++    """
++    p = clean_path(path)
++    if not p:
++        return False
++    return os.path.isabs(p) or p[0] in ("/", "\\")
++
++
++def path_key(path: str) -> str:
++    """Normalised, case-folded key for comparing two paths."""
++    return os.path.normcase(os.path.normpath(clean_path(path)))
++
++
++def to_db_path(full_path: str, base_dir: str) -> str:
++    """Return full_path relative to base_dir (forward slashes) when inside it.
++
++    Paths outside base_dir (or on another drive) are returned unchanged.
++    """
++    if not full_path or not base_dir:
++        return full_path
++    try:
++        abs_full = os.path.abspath(full_path)
++        abs_base = os.path.abspath(base_dir)
++        nf = os.path.normcase(os.path.normpath(abs_full))
++        nb = os.path.normcase(os.path.normpath(abs_base))
++        if nf == nb or os.path.commonpath([nf, nb]) != nb:
++            return full_path
++        return os.path.relpath(abs_full, abs_base).replace("\\", "/")
++    except (ValueError, OSError):
++        return full_path
++
++
++def unique_destination(dest: str, claimed: set[str], src: str | None = None) -> str:
++    """Return dest, or dest with _2, _3 ... appended to the stem, such that the
++    result neither exists on disk (unless it is src itself) nor was already
++    claimed by another record in the current batch.  The result is claimed."""
++
++    def taken(p: str) -> bool:
++        if path_key(p) in claimed:
++            return True
++        if os.path.exists(p):
++            try:
++                if src and os.path.exists(src) and os.path.samefile(src, p):
++                    return False
++            except OSError:
++                pass
++            return True
++        return False
++
++    stem, ext = os.path.splitext(dest)
++    cand, n = dest, 2
++    while taken(cand):
++        cand = f"{stem}_{n}{ext}"
++        n += 1
++    claimed.add(path_key(cand))
++    return cand
++
++
++def relocate_file(src: str, dest: str, copy: bool = False) -> tuple[bool, str]:
++    """Move or copy src to dest WITHOUT ever overwriting an existing file.
++
++    Returns (ok, error_message).  ok is also True when dest already is the
++    same file as src.
++    """
++    try:
++        if os.path.exists(dest):
++            try:
++                same = os.path.samefile(src, dest)
++            except OSError:
++                same = False
++            if not same:
++                return False, "destination already exists"
++            if not copy and os.path.basename(src) != os.path.basename(dest):
++                os.rename(src, dest)  # case-only rename on a case-insensitive FS
++            return True, ""
++        parent = os.path.dirname(dest)
++        if parent:
++            os.makedirs(parent, exist_ok=True)
++        if copy:
++            shutil.copy2(src, dest)
++        else:
++            shutil.move(src, dest)
++        return True, ""
++    except Exception as err:  # noqa: BLE001 - report any OS/shutil error
++        return False, str(err)
++
++
++def build_basename_index(base_dir: str, limit: int = 50000) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
++    """Map lower-cased file name -> full paths for every file below base_dir."""
++    index: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
++    seen = 0
++    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(base_dir):
++        dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if not d.startswith(".")]
++        for fname in files:
++            if fname.startswith("."):
++                continue
++            index.setdefault(fname.lower(), []).append(os.path.join(root, fname))
++            seen += 1
++            if seen >= limit:
++                return index
++    return index
