+
+"""Database repair engine for the GWizard citation fix tool (no GUI)."""
+
+# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
+#
+# Standard Python modules
+#
+# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
+from __future__ import annotations
+import logging
+import re
+from collections import defaultdict
+from typing import Any
+
+# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
+#
+# Gramps modules
+#
+# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
+from gramps.gen.const import GRAMPS_LOCALE as glocale
+from gramps.gen.db import DbTxn
+from gramps.gen.lib import (
+    Note,
+    NoteType,
+    Repository,
+    RepositoryType,
+    RepoRef,
+    Url,
+    UrlType,
+)
+from gramps.plugins.tool.gw_goldstandardrepos import GoldStandardRepositories
+from gramps.plugins.tool.gwizardcitationshared import (
+    clean_source_title,
+    detect_title_elements,
+    is_debris_text,
+    is_tree_source_title,
+    normalize_repo_name,
+    normalize_source_title,
+    note_text,
+    split_conflated_title,
+    unpacked_abbreviation,
+)
+
+_ = glocale.translation.sgettext
+LOG = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+# Gold-standard "type" text -> Gramps repository type constant.
+_GOLD_REPO_TYPES = {
+    "Web site": RepositoryType.WEBSITE,
+    "Archive": RepositoryType.ARCHIVE,
+    "Library": RepositoryType.LIBRARY,
+    "Collection": RepositoryType.COLLECTION,
+    "Government Office": RepositoryType.ARCHIVE,
+}
+
+
+# ------------------------------------------------------------
+#
+# GWizardCitationRepairEngine
+#
+# ------------------------------------------------------------
+class GWizardCitationRepairEngine:
+    """Safe database transformations for each step of the citation fix tool.
+
+    Every public method that changes the database does so inside one
+    DbTxn, so a whole step can be undone with Edit > Undo. Methods that
+    take a ``trans`` argument join that transaction instead of opening
+    their own, so callers can group several operations into one undo.
+    """
+
+    last_abbreviations_updated: int = 0
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------
+    # Step 1: unpack conflated source titles
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------
+    def plan_unpack_conflated_sources(self, db: Any) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
+        """Return the proposed splits without touching the database."""
+        plan: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
+        for source in db.iter_sources():
+            title = str(source.get_title() or "")
+            if len(detect_title_elements(title)) < 2:
+                continue
+            result = split_conflated_title(title)
+            if result is None:
+                continue
+            plan.append(
+                {
+                    "handle": source.get_handle(),
+                    "gramps_id": str(source.get_gramps_id() or ""),
+                    "old_title": title,
+                    "repo_name": result["repo_name"],
+                    "new_title": result["new_title"],
+                    "moved_text": result["moved_text"],
+                    "apply": True,
+                }
+            )
+        # Titles with markup, citation-style quotes or a bare website address
+        # are cleaned too, for sources the split above did not already plan.
+        planned = {str(item["handle"]) for item in plan}
+        for source in db.iter_sources():
+            handle = str(source.get_handle())
+            if handle in planned:
+                continue
+            old_title = str(source.get_title() or "")
+            new_title, moved, repo_name, reason = clean_source_title(old_title)
+            if not new_title and not moved and not repo_name:
+                continue
+            plan.append(
+                {
+                    "handle": handle,
+                    "gramps_id": str(source.get_gramps_id() or ""),
+                    "old_title": old_title,
+                    "repo_name": repo_name,
+                    "new_title": new_title or old_title.strip(),
+                    "moved_text": moved,
+                    "reason": reason,
+                    "apply": True,
+                }
+            )
+        return plan
+
+    def apply_unpack_plan(self, db: Any, plan: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> int:
+        """Apply the entries of an unpack plan that are marked ``apply``."""
+        return self.apply_unpack_entries(
+            db, [entry for entry in plan if entry.get("apply", True)]
+        )
+
+    def apply_unpack_entries(
+        self, db: Any, entries: list[dict[str, Any]], trans: Any = None
+    ) -> int:
+        """Apply unpack entries; the one implementation used by every caller.
+
+        Each entry holds ``handle`` and any of ``repo_name``, ``new_title``
+        and ``moved_text``. A blank field is left alone, so the review
+        dialog (which may leave some target columns empty) and the
+        no-review path behave identically. Returns the number of sources
+        changed.
+        """
+        if trans is None:
+            self.last_abbreviations_updated = 0
+            with DbTxn(_("Unpack Conflated Source"), db) as new_trans:
+                return self.apply_unpack_entries(db, entries, new_trans)
+        repo_map: dict[str, str] = {}
+        for repo in db.iter_repositories():
+            key = normalize_repo_name(str(repo.get_name() or ""))
+            if key:
+                repo_map.setdefault(key, repo.get_handle())
+
+        count = 0
+        for entry in entries:
+            repo_name = str(entry.get("repo_name") or "").strip()
+            new_title = str(entry.get("new_title") or "").strip()
+            moved = str(entry.get("moved_text") or "").strip()
+            if not repo_name and not new_title and not moved:
+                continue
+            try:
+                source = db.get_source_from_handle(entry["handle"])
+                if source is None:
+                    continue
+                before = source.serialize()
+                # A title-only entry (markup or quotes) has no repository.
+                if repo_name:
+                    key = normalize_repo_name(repo_name)
+                    repo_handle = repo_map.get(key)
+                    if not repo_handle:
+                        repo_handle = self._create_repository(db, repo_name, trans)
+                        repo_map[key] = repo_handle
+                    linked = any(
+                        ref.get_reference_handle() == repo_handle
+                        for ref in source.get_reporef_list()
+                    )
+                    if not linked:
+                        repo_ref = RepoRef()
+                        repo_ref.set_reference_handle(repo_handle)
+                        source.add_repo_reference(repo_ref)
+                if new_title:
+                    new_abbrev = unpacked_abbreviation(
+                        str(source.get_abbreviation() or ""),
+                        str(source.get_title() or ""),
+                        new_title,
+                        repo_name,
+                    )
+                    source.set_title(new_title)
+                    if new_abbrev is not None:
+                        source.set_abbreviation(new_abbrev)
+                        self.last_abbreviations_updated += 1
+                if moved:
+                    pubinfo = str(source.get_publication_info() or "").strip()
+                    source.set_publication_info(
+                        "%s; %s" % (pubinfo, moved) if pubinfo else moved
+                    )
+                if source.serialize() == before:
+                    continue  # already unpacked; leave it alone
+                db.commit_source(source, trans)
+                count += 1
+            except Exception:  # pylint: disable=broad-except
+                LOG.exception("Failed to unpack source %s", entry.get("handle"))
+        return count
+
+    def unpack_conflated_sources(self, db: Any) -> int:
+        """Plan and apply the unpack step with no review."""
+        return self.apply_unpack_plan(db, self.plan_unpack_conflated_sources(db))
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _create_repository(db: Any, name: str, trans: Any) -> str:
+        """Add a repository, filling type and URL for gold-standard names."""
+        repo = Repository()
+        repo.set_name(name)
+        gold = GoldStandardRepositories.get_by_name(name)
+        if gold:
+            repo_type = _GOLD_REPO_TYPES.get(gold.get("type", ""))
+            if repo_type is not None:
+                repo.set_type(repo_type)
+            if str(gold.get("url") or "").startswith(("http://", "https://")):
+                url = Url()
+                url.set_path(gold["url"])
+                url.set_type(UrlType.WEB_HOME)
+                repo.add_url(url)
+        db.add_repository(repo, trans)
+        return repo.get_handle()
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------
+    # Step 2: repositories
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------
+    def merge_repositories(
+        self, db: Any, keeper_handle: str, discard_handle: str, trans: Any = None
+    ) -> bool:
+        """Merge one repository into another, re-pointing every source."""
+        if trans is None:
+            with DbTxn(_("Merge repositories"), db) as new_trans:
+                return self.merge_repositories(
+                    db, keeper_handle, discard_handle, new_trans
+                )
+        if keeper_handle == discard_handle:
+            return False
+        keeper = db.get_repository_from_handle(keeper_handle)
+        discard = db.get_repository_from_handle(discard_handle)
+        if keeper is None or discard is None:
+            return False
+        for _cls, source_handle in list(
+            db.find_backlink_handles(discard_handle, ["Source"])
+        ):
+            source = db.get_source_from_handle(source_handle)
+            if source is not None:
+                source.replace_repo_references(discard_handle, keeper_handle)
+                db.commit_source(source, trans)
+        keeper.merge(discard)
+        db.commit_repository(keeper, trans)
+        db.remove_repository(discard_handle, trans)
+        return True
+
+    def consolidate_duplicate_repositories(self, db: Any) -> int:
+        """Merge repositories whose names normalize to the same text.
+
+        Name-only scripting helper. The GUI steps use the hint-based
+        ``auto_consolidate_repositories`` in gw_repoconsolidatedialog instead.
+        """
+        groups: dict[str, list[Any]] = defaultdict(list)
+        for repo in db.iter_repositories():
+            key = normalize_repo_name(str(repo.get_name() or ""))
+            if key:
+                groups[key].append(repo)
+
+        golden_names = set(GoldStandardRepositories.get_names())
+
+        def rank(repo: Any) -> tuple[Any, ...]:
+            uses = len(list(db.find_backlink_handles(repo.get_handle(), ["Source"])))
+            return (
+                str(repo.get_name() or "") not in golden_names,
+                -uses,
+                str(repo.get_gramps_id() or ""),
+            )
+
+        merged = 0
+        with DbTxn(_("Consolidate Repositories"), db) as trans:
+            for group in groups.values():
+                if len(group) < 2:
+                    continue
+                group.sort(key=rank)
+                keeper = group[0]
+                for duplicate in group[1:]:
+                    if self.merge_repositories(
+                        db, keeper.get_handle(), duplicate.get_handle(), trans
+                    ):
+                        merged += 1
+            self.apply_gold_standard_details(db, trans)
+        return merged
+
+    def apply_gold_standard_details(self, db: Any, trans: Any = None) -> int:
+        """Give repositories matching the golden list its type and web address.
+
+        GEDCOM carries no repository type, so imported repositories all start
+        as Gramps' default (Library). Only that default is replaced; a type
+        you chose yourself is never overwritten, and existing URLs are kept.
+        """
+        if trans is None:
+            with DbTxn(_("Apply Gold Standard Repository Details"), db) as new_trans:
+                return self.apply_gold_standard_details(db, new_trans)
+        catalog = {
+            normalize_repo_name(entry["name"]): entry
+            for entry in GoldStandardRepositories.get_all()
+        }
+        changed = 0
+        for repo in list(db.iter_repositories()):
+            entry = catalog.get(normalize_repo_name(str(repo.get_name() or "")))
+            if entry is None:
+                continue
+            modified = False
+            wanted = _GOLD_REPO_TYPES.get(entry.get("type", ""))
+            if (
+                wanted is not None
+                and repo.get_type().value == RepositoryType.LIBRARY
+                and wanted != RepositoryType.LIBRARY
+            ):
+                repo.set_type(wanted)
+                modified = True
+            url_text = str(entry.get("url") or "")
+            if url_text.startswith(("http://", "https://")) and not repo.get_url_list():
+                url = Url()
+                url.set_path(url_text)
+                url.set_type(UrlType.WEB_HOME)
+                repo.add_url(url)
+                modified = True
+            if modified:
+                db.commit_repository(repo, trans)
+                changed += 1
+        return changed
+
+    def reassign_source_repositories(
+        self, db: Any, changes: list[dict[str, str]], trans: Any = None
+    ) -> tuple[int, int]:
+        """Point individual sources at the repositories chosen for them.
+
+        Each change is ``{"source_handle", "old_repo_handle", "target_name"}``.
+        ``old_repo_handle`` is the repository the row currently shows (empty
+        for a source that has none). The target repository is found by name
+        (ignoring case and punctuation) and created, with the type and web
+        address from the golden list, when it does not exist yet.
+
+        Returns ``(sources changed, repositories created)``.
+        """
+        if trans is None:
+            with DbTxn(_("Change Source Repositories"), db) as new_trans:
+                return self.reassign_source_repositories(db, changes, new_trans)
+        repo_map: dict[str, str] = {}
+        for repo in db.iter_repositories():
+            key = normalize_repo_name(str(repo.get_name() or ""))
+            if key:
+                repo_map.setdefault(key, repo.get_handle())
+
+        changed = 0
+        created = 0
+        for change in changes:
+            target = str(change.get("target_name") or "").strip()
+            if not target:
+                continue
+            try:
+                source = db.get_source_from_handle(change["source_handle"])
+                if source is None:
+                    continue
+                key = normalize_repo_name(target)
+                new_handle = repo_map.get(key)
+                if not new_handle:
+                    new_handle = self._create_repository(db, target, trans)
+                    repo_map[key] = new_handle
+                    created += 1
+                old_handle = str(change.get("old_repo_handle") or "")
+                if old_handle == new_handle:
+                    continue
+                current = [
+                    ref.get_reference_handle() for ref in source.get_reporef_list()
+                ]
+                if old_handle and old_handle in current:
+                    source.replace_repo_references(old_handle, new_handle)
+                elif new_handle not in current:
+                    repo_ref = RepoRef()
+                    repo_ref.set_reference_handle(new_handle)
+                    source.add_repo_reference(repo_ref)
+                else:
+                    continue
+                db.commit_source(source, trans)
+                changed += 1
+            except Exception:  # pylint: disable=broad-except
+                LOG.exception(
+                    "Failed to change repository of source %s",
+                    change.get("source_handle"),
+                )
+        return changed, created
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------
+    # Step 3: sources
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------
+    def merge_sources(
+        self, db: Any, keeper_handle: str, discard_handle: str, trans: Any = None
+    ) -> bool:
+        """Merge one source into another, re-pointing every citation."""
+        if trans is None:
+            with DbTxn(_("Merge sources"), db) as new_trans:
+                return self.merge_sources(db, keeper_handle, discard_handle, new_trans)
+        if keeper_handle == discard_handle:
+            return False
+        try:
+            keeper = db.get_source_from_handle(keeper_handle)
+        except Exception:
+            keeper = None
+        try:
+            discard = db.get_source_from_handle(discard_handle)
+        except Exception:
+            discard = None
+        if keeper is None or discard is None:
+            return False
+        for _cls, citation_handle in list(
+            db.find_backlink_handles(discard_handle, ["Citation"])
+        ):
+            citation = db.get_citation_from_handle(citation_handle)
+            if citation is not None:
+                citation.set_reference_handle(keeper_handle)
+                db.commit_citation(citation, trans)
+        keeper.merge(discard)
+        # Source.merge keeps notes, media, tags and repositories but not the
+        # text fields, so fill any the keeper lacks from the discarded source.
+        if not str(keeper.get_author() or "").strip() and discard.get_author():
+            keeper.set_author(discard.get_author())
+        if (
+            not str(keeper.get_publication_info() or "").strip()
+            and discard.get_publication_info()
+        ):
+            keeper.set_publication_info(discard.get_publication_info())
+        if (
+            not str(keeper.get_abbreviation() or "").strip()
+            and discard.get_abbreviation()
+        ):
+            keeper.set_abbreviation(discard.get_abbreviation())
+        # Where both sources had text and it differs, the discarded wording
+        # would vanish. Keep it in a note on the surviving source instead.
+        self._keep_conflicting_source_text(db, keeper, discard, trans)
+        LOG.info(
+            "Merged source %s '%s' into %s '%s'",
+            discard.get_gramps_id(),
+            discard.get_title(),
+            keeper.get_gramps_id(),
+            keeper.get_title(),
+        )
+        db.commit_source(keeper, trans)
+        db.remove_source(discard_handle, trans)
+        return True
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _keep_conflicting_source_text(
+        db: Any, keeper: Any, discard: Any, trans: Any
+    ) -> bool:
+        """Add a note to ``keeper`` holding discarded text that differs.
+
+        Compares author, publication info and abbreviation (ignoring case
+        and spacing). Nothing is added when the fields agree or when the
+        keeper had no text of its own (that case is copied across instead).
+        Returns True when a note was added.
+        """
+
+        def squash(text: Any) -> str:
+            return " ".join(str(text or "").split()).casefold()
+
+        fields = (
+            (_("Author"), keeper.get_author, discard.get_author),
+            (
+                _("Publication info"),
+                keeper.get_publication_info,
+                discard.get_publication_info,
+            ),
+            (_("Abbreviation"), keeper.get_abbreviation, discard.get_abbreviation),
+        )
+        lost: list[str] = []
+        for label, get_keep, get_drop in fields:
+            kept_text = " ".join(str(get_keep() or "").split())
+            dropped_text = " ".join(str(get_drop() or "").split())
+            if dropped_text and kept_text and squash(kept_text) != squash(dropped_text):
+                lost.append("%s: %s" % (label, dropped_text))
+        if not lost:
+            return False
+        text = str(
+            _(
+                "Merged from source %(gid)s '%(title)s'. Text not kept in "
+                "the fields above:\n%(lost)s"
+            )
+        ) % {
+            "gid": str(discard.get_gramps_id() or ""),
+            "title": str(discard.get_title() or ""),
+            "lost": "\n".join(lost),
+        }
+        for note_handle in keeper.get_note_list():
+            existing = db.get_note_from_handle(note_handle)
+            if existing is not None and existing.get() == text:
+                return False
+        note = Note()
+        note.set(text)
+        note.set_type(NoteType.SOURCE)
+        keeper.add_note(db.add_note(note, trans))
+        return True
+
+    def consolidate_duplicate_sources(self, db: Any) -> int:
+        """Merge sources whose titles normalize to the same text.
+
+        Title-only scripting helper. The GUI steps use the hint-based
+        ``auto_fix_sources`` in gw_sourcesfixdialog instead.
+        """
+        groups: dict[str, list[Any]] = defaultdict(list)
+        for source in db.iter_sources():
+            key = normalize_source_title(str(source.get_title() or ""))
+            if key:
+                groups[key].append(source)
+
+        def rank(source: Any) -> tuple[Any, ...]:
+            cites = len(
+                list(db.find_backlink_handles(source.get_handle(), ["Citation"]))
+            )
+            return (
+                -len(list(source.get_reporef_list())),
+                -int(bool(re.search(r"\bU\.S\.", str(source.get_title() or "")))),
+                -cites,
+                str(source.get_gramps_id() or ""),
+            )
+
+        merged = 0
+        with DbTxn(_("Consolidate Sources"), db) as trans:
+            for group in groups.values():
+                if len(group) < 2:
+                    continue
+                group.sort(key=rank)
+                keeper = group[0]
+                for duplicate in group[1:]:
+                    if self.merge_sources(
+                        db, keeper.get_handle(), duplicate.get_handle(), trans
+                    ):
+                        merged += 1
+        return merged
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------
+    # Step 4: citations
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------
+    def clean_and_rate_citations(self, db: Any) -> int:
+        """Downrate user-tree citations and tidy the Volume/Page text.
+
+        Scripting helper. The GUI steps use ``auto_fix_citations`` in
+        gw_citationsfixdialog instead.
+        """
+        tree_handles = {
+            str(src.get_handle())
+            for src in db.iter_sources()
+            if is_tree_source_title(str(src.get_title() or ""))
+        }
+        fixed = 0
+        with DbTxn(_("Clean Citations and Confidence"), db) as trans:
+            for citation in list(db.iter_citations()):
+                modified = False
+                if str(citation.get_reference_handle() or "") in tree_handles:
+                    # Gramps confidence: 0 Very Low ... 4 Very High. User trees
+                    # are lowered to Low (1), the same as the Fix Citations
+                    # dialog.
+                    if int(citation.get_confidence_level()) >= 3:
+                        citation.set_confidence_level(1)
+                        modified = True
+                page = str(citation.get_page() or "")
+                if page:
+                    cleaned = re.sub(r"^[,\.\s;]+|[,\.\s;]+$", "", page.strip())
+                    cleaned = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", cleaned)
+                    if cleaned != page:
+                        citation.set_page(cleaned)
+                        modified = True
+                if modified:
+                    db.commit_citation(citation, trans)
+                    fixed += 1
+        return fixed
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------
+    # Step 5: notes
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------
+    def purge_import_debris_notes(self, db: Any) -> int:
+        """Remove import-debris notes and every reference to them.
+
+        Scripting helper. The GUI steps use ``auto_fix_notes`` in
+        gw_notesfixdialog instead.
+        """
+        purged = 0
+        with DbTxn(_("Purge Import Debris Notes"), db) as trans:
+            for note in list(db.iter_notes()):
+                if not is_debris_text(note_text(note).strip()):
+                    continue
+                note_handle = note.get_handle()
+                for cls_name, parent_handle in list(
+                    db.find_backlink_handles(note_handle)
+                ):
+                    getter = getattr(db, "get_%s_from_handle" % cls_name.lower(), None)
+                    commit = getattr(db, "commit_%s" % cls_name.lower(), None)
+                    if getter is None or commit is None:
+                        LOG.warning("Cannot detach note from %s", cls_name)
+                        continue
+                    parent = getter(parent_handle)
+                    if parent is not None:
+                        parent.remove_handle_references("Note", [note_handle])
+                        commit(parent, trans)
+                db.remove_note(note_handle, trans)
+                purged += 1
+        return purged

+"""Database scanning and report text for the GWizard citation fix tool."""

+# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
+#
+# Standard Python modules
+#
+# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
+from __future__ import annotations
+import logging
+import os
+import re
+import traceback
+from collections import Counter, defaultdict
+from typing import Any
+
+# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
+#
+# Gramps modules
+#
+# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
+from gramps.plugins.tool.gwizardcitationshared import (
+    detect_title_elements,
+    is_debris_text,
+    is_tree_source_title,
+    normalize_source_title,
+    note_text,
+)
+
+LOG = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+LONG_NOTE_CHARS = 2000
+
+# --- Heuristics used by the placement / hygiene checks ----------------------
+_MARKUP_RE = re.compile(r"</?[A-Za-z][^<>]*>")
+_ACCESS_RE = re.compile(
+    r"\b(?:accessed|viewed|retrieved|downloaded)\s+(?:on\s+)?"
+    r"(?:\d{1,2}\s+[A-Za-z]{3,9}\.?\s+\d{4}|[A-Za-z]{3,9}\.?\s+\d{1,2},?\s+\d{4})",
+    re.IGNORECASE,
+)
+_YEAR_RANGE_RE = re.compile(r"\b\d{4}\s*[-\u2013]\s*(?:\d{4}|current|present)\b", re.I)
+_URL_RE = re.compile(r"^(?:https?://|www\.)", re.IGNORECASE)
+_FILENAME_RE = re.compile(r"\.(?:jpe?g|png|gif|tiff?|bmp|pdf|docx?|txt|html?)$", re.I)
+_DOMAIN_RE = re.compile(r"^[\w-]+(?:\.[\w-]+)+$")
+_PLACEHOLDER_TITLES = {"", "unknown", "untitled", "none", "n/a", "na", "source"}
+# Words that suggest text names a collection/record set (source-level data).
+_COLLECTION_WORDS = re.compile(
+    r"\b(index|indexes|indices|records?|registry|registries|collection|"
+    r"lists?|crossings|manifests?|database|census|certificates)\b",
+    re.IGNORECASE,
+)
+# Words that suggest real pinpoint detail (citation-level data).
+_PINPOINT_WORDS = re.compile(
+    r"\b(sheet|line|page|pg|pp?\.|enumeration|ed|roll|frame|image|film|folio|"
+    r"book|volume|vol|number|no\.|entry|person id|item|certificate (?:no|number)|"
+    r"plot|section|lot)\b|#",
+    re.IGNORECASE,
+)
+
+
+def _page_template(page: str) -> str:
+    """Collapse names, ids, dates and numbers so look-alike pages group together."""
+    text = " ".join((page or "").split())
+    text = re.sub(r"person ID [A-Z0-9]{3,5}-[A-Z0-9]{2,5}", "person ID <ID>", text)
+    text = re.sub(r"entry for [^,]+,", "entry for <NAME>,", text)
+    text = re.sub(r"\b\d{1,2}\s+[A-Za-z]{3,9}\.?\s+\d{4}\b", "<DATE>", text)
+    text = re.sub(r"\d+", "#", text)
+    return text
+
+
+# Lowercase words that properly start a page: Evidence Explained style
+# "entry for ...", and pinpoint detail such as "page 5" or "roll 12".
+_LEGIT_LOWER_START = re.compile(
+    r"^(?:entry|page|pages|pg|pp?\.|sheet|roll|frame|image|film|folio|vol|"
+    r"volume|book|line|item|plot|section|lot|no\.|number|digital|record)\b",
+    re.IGNORECASE,
+)
+
+
+def _page_is_fragment(page: str) -> bool:
+    """True if the text looks cut off at the start (begins lowercase, or has a
+    closing parenthesis before any opening one).
+
+    A web address and the usual lowercase openers ("entry for ...",
+    "page 5") are complete values, not fragments.
+    """
+    text = (page or "").strip()
+    if not text:
+        return False
+    if _URL_RE.match(text):
+        return False
+    if text[0].islower():
+        return not _LEGIT_LOWER_START.match(text)
+    close, opened = text.find(")"), text.find("(")
+    return close != -1 and (opened == -1 or close < opened)
+
+
+def _page_looks_like_source_text(page: str) -> bool:
+    """Collection-style wording with no pinpoint detail: probably belongs in the
+    source title, not the citation page."""
+    text = (page or "").strip()
+    if not text or _ACCESS_RE.search(text) or _URL_RE.match(text):
+        return False
+    return bool(_COLLECTION_WORDS.search(text)) and not _PINPOINT_WORDS.search(text)
+
+
+def _strip_the(text: str) -> str:
+    low = " ".join((text or "").lower().split())
+    return low[4:] if low.startswith("the ") else low
+
+
+def _loose_key(title: str, strip_year_ranges: bool = False) -> str:
+    """Very forgiving title key: case, punctuation, '&', 'U.S.' and 'the' ignored."""
+    text = (title or "").lower().replace("&", " and ")
+    if strip_year_ranges:
+        text = _YEAR_RANGE_RE.sub(" ", text)
+    tokens = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", " ", text).split()
+    return " ".join(t for t in tokens if t not in ("u", "s", "the"))
+
+
+def _title_problems(text: str) -> list[str]:
+    """Hygiene problems in a source title/author/publication string."""
+    problems = []
+    if _MARKUP_RE.search(text):
+        problems.append("html markup")
+    if text != text.strip() or "  " in text:
+        problems.append("stray whitespace")
+    stripped = text.strip()
+    if stripped[:1] in ('"', "'", "\u201c") and len(stripped) > 1:
+        problems.append("leading quote mark")
+    return problems
+
+
+def _known_site_names() -> set[str]:
+    """Return lower-cased gold-standard repository names ("Legacy.com")."""
+    try:
+        from gramps.plugins.tool.gw_goldstandardrepos import GoldStandardRepositories
+
+        return {name.casefold() for name in GoldStandardRepositories.get_names()}
+    except Exception:  # pylint: disable=broad-except
+        return set()
+
+
+def kind_of_non_title(title: str) -> str:
+    """Return 'url', 'filename', 'domain' when the title is not a real title.
+
+    A proper site name that merely looks like a domain ("Legacy.com") is a
+    real title, so names of known repositories are not flagged.
+    """
+    t = (title or "").strip()
+    if _URL_RE.match(t):
+        return "url"
+    if _FILENAME_RE.search(t):
+        return "filename"
+    if " " not in t and _DOMAIN_RE.match(t) and t.casefold() not in _known_site_names():
+        return "domain"
+    return ""
+
+
+_kind_of_non_title = kind_of_non_title  # backward-compatible private name
+
+
+class _ScanErrors:
+    """Collects exceptions raised by Gramps methods during a scan.
+
+    Identical failures are grouped (same step, same function, same message) so
+    one broken method on 3,000 citations gives one line with a count and one
+    example id, not 3,000 lines. Only the first of each kind goes to the log.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self._groups: dict[tuple[str, str, str, str], dict[str, Any]] = {}
+
+    def record(self, where: str, exc: BaseException, obj: Any = None) -> None:
+        try:
+            frames = traceback.extract_tb(exc.__traceback__)
+            func = frames[-1].name if frames else "?"
+        except Exception:  # pylint: disable=broad-except
+            func = "?"
+        message = " ".join(str(exc).split())[:120]
+        key = (where, func, type(exc).__name__, message)
+        group = self._groups.get(key)
+        if group is None:
+            group = {
+                "where": where,
+                "function": func,
+                "error_type": type(exc).__name__,
+                "message": message,
+                "count": 0,
+                "example": self._describe(obj),
+            }
+            self._groups[key] = group
+            LOG.warning(
+                "GWizard report: %s failed in %s: %s: %s",
+                where,
+                func,
+                group["error_type"],
+                message,
+                exc_info=exc,
+            )
+        group["count"] += 1
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _describe(obj: Any) -> str:
+        """Best-effort id of the object being inspected; must never raise."""
+        if obj is None:
+            return ""
+        for name in ("get_gramps_id", "get_handle"):
+            try:
+                value = getattr(obj, name)()
+                if value:
+                    return str(value)
+            except Exception:  # pylint: disable=broad-except
+                pass
+        return ""
+
+    def as_list(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
+        return sorted(self._groups.values(), key=lambda g: -g["count"])
+
+
+class GWizardCitationReport:
+    """Handles the algorithmic parsing, database scanning, and text generation."""
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self._errors = _ScanErrors()
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def normalize_source_title(title: str) -> str:
+        return normalize_source_title(title)
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _person_has_citation(person: Any, db: Any = None, errors: Any = None) -> bool:
+        """True when the person, a name, or one of their events has a citation."""
+        try:
+            if person.get_citation_list():
+                return True
+            names = [person.get_primary_name()] + list(person.get_alternate_names())
+            if any(name.get_citation_list() for name in names):
+                return True
+            if db is not None:
+                for ref in person.get_event_ref_list():
+                    event = db.get_event_from_handle(ref.ref)
+                    if event is not None and event.get_citation_list():
+                        return True
+        except Exception as exc:  # pylint: disable=broad-except
+            if errors is not None:
+                errors.record("people: citation check", exc, person)
+            else:
+                LOG.exception("Failed to inspect person citations")
+        return False
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _note_text(note: Any) -> str:
+        return note_text(note)
+
+    def collect_placement_stats(
+        self,
+        sources: list[Any],
+        citations: list[Any],
+        repos: list[Any],
+        cites_by_source: Counter,
+        near_duplicates: list[list[dict[str, Any]]],
+    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        """Checks for data sitting in the wrong field and for source hygiene.
+
+        Read-only: nothing is modified. Each result is a plain list/dict so the
+        dialogs can reuse it later.
+        """
+        out: dict[str, Any] = {}
+        src_by_handle = {str(s.get_handle()): s for s in sources}
+
+        def _label(src: Any) -> str:
+            return "%s '%s'" % (src.get_gramps_id(), str(src.get_title() or ""))
+
+        # --- Source field hygiene ---------------------------------------
+        markup_sources, citation_style, non_titles, placeholders = [], [], [], []
+        for src in sources:
+            try:
+                title = str(src.get_title() or "")
+                fields = {
+                    "title": title,
+                    "author": str(src.get_author() or ""),
+                    "publication": str(src.get_publication_info() or ""),
+                    "abbreviation": str(src.get_abbreviation() or ""),
+                }
+                row = {
+                    "gramps_id": str(src.get_gramps_id() or ""),
+                    "title": title,
+                    "citations": cites_by_source.get(str(src.get_handle()), 0),
+                }
+                bad = {
+                    name: _title_problems(text)
+                    for name, text in fields.items()
+                    if text and _title_problems(text)
+                }
+                if bad:
+                    markup_sources.append(dict(row, problems=bad))
+                low = title.lower()
+                if len(title) > 40 and (
+                    "database," in low or '",' in title or "(http" in low
+                ):
+                    citation_style.append(row)
+                kind = _kind_of_non_title(title)
+                if kind:
+                    non_titles.append(dict(row, kind=kind))
+                if low.strip() in _PLACEHOLDER_TITLES:
+                    placeholders.append(row)
+            except Exception as exc:  # pylint: disable=broad-except
+                self._errors.record("sources: field checks", exc, src)
+        out["sources_bad_fields"] = markup_sources
+        out["sources_citation_style"] = citation_style
+        out["sources_non_titles"] = non_titles
+        out["sources_placeholder"] = placeholders
+        out["sources_unused"] = [
+            {
+                "gramps_id": str(s.get_gramps_id() or ""),
+                "title": str(s.get_title() or ""),
+            }
+            for s in sources
+            if cites_by_source.get(str(s.get_handle()), 0) == 0
+        ]
+
+        # --- Citation text placement ------------------------------------
+        templates: Counter = Counter()
+        fragments: Counter = Counter()  # source label -> count
+        access_in_page = 0
+        access_in_page_no_date = 0
+        source_like_pages: dict[str, set] = defaultdict(set)
+        empty_cits = 0
+        empty_by_source: Counter = Counter()
+        distinct_pages = set()
+        for cit in citations:
+            try:
+                page = (cit.get_page() or "").strip()
+                src = src_by_handle.get(str(cit.get_reference_handle()))
+                label = _label(src) if src is not None else "(missing source)"
+                has_date = not cit.get_date_object().is_empty()
+                if page:
+                    distinct_pages.add(page)
+                    templates[_page_template(page)] += 1
+                    if _page_is_fragment(page):
+                        fragments[label] += 1
+                    if _ACCESS_RE.search(page):
+                        access_in_page += 1
+                        if not has_date:
+                            access_in_page_no_date += 1
+                    if _page_looks_like_source_text(page):
+                        source_like_pages[label].add(page)
+                if not (
+                    page
+                    or has_date
+                    or cit.get_attribute_list()
+                    or cit.get_note_list()
+                    or cit.get_media_list()
+                ):
+                    empty_cits += 1
+                    empty_by_source[label] += 1
+            except Exception as exc:  # pylint: disable=broad-except
+                self._errors.record("citations: page/date/empty checks", exc, cit)
+                continue
+        out["page_distinct"] = len(distinct_pages)
+        out["page_templates"] = templates.most_common(5)
+        out["page_fragments"] = fragments.most_common()
+        out["page_access_dates"] = access_in_page
+        out["page_access_dates_no_date"] = access_in_page_no_date
+        out["page_source_like"] = {k: sorted(v) for k, v in source_like_pages.items()}
+        out["citations_empty"] = empty_cits
+        out["citations_empty_by_source"] = empty_by_source.most_common(5)
+
+        # --- Duplicate sources the strict title match misses ------------
+        known = [frozenset(r["gramps_id"] for r in g) for g in near_duplicates]
+        rows = []
+        for src in sources:
+            rows.append(
+                {
+                    "gramps_id": str(src.get_gramps_id() or ""),
+                    "title": str(src.get_title() or ""),
+                }
+            )
+
+        def _groups(strip: bool) -> list[list[dict[str, Any]]]:
+            buckets: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = defaultdict(list)
+            for row in rows:
+                key = _loose_key(row["title"], strip)
+                if key and row["title"].strip().lower() not in _PLACEHOLDER_TITLES:
+                    buckets[key].append(row)
+            return [g for g in buckets.values() if len(g) > 1]
+
+        safe = [
+            g
+            for g in _groups(False)
+            if frozenset(r["gramps_id"] for r in g) not in known
+        ]
+        safe_sets = known + [frozenset(r["gramps_id"] for r in g) for g in safe]
+        versions = [
+            g
+            for g in _groups(True)
+            if frozenset(r["gramps_id"] for r in g) not in safe_sets
+        ]
+        out["dupes_loose"] = safe  # same title once 'U.S.' etc. is ignored
+        out["dupes_year_variants"] = versions  # same title, different year range
+
+        # --- Repository hygiene -----------------------------------------
+        used_repos = set()
+        for src in sources:
+            try:
+                for ref in src.get_reporef_list():
+                    used_repos.add(str(ref.ref))
+            except Exception as exc:  # pylint: disable=broad-except
+                self._errors.record("sources: repository links", exc, src)
+                continue
+        repo_unused, repo_dup_addr, repo_packed_name = [], [], []
+        for repo in repos:
+            try:
+                name = str(repo.get_name() or "")
+                rid = str(repo.get_gramps_id() or "")
+                if str(repo.get_handle()) not in used_repos:
+                    repo_unused.append({"gramps_id": rid, "name": name})
+                for addr in repo.get_address_list():
+                    street = str(addr.get_street() or "").strip()
+                    if street and _strip_the(street) == _strip_the(name):
+                        repo_dup_addr.append({"gramps_id": rid, "name": name})
+                        break
+                    if street and (
+                        len(street) > 60
+                        or (
+                            len(street) > len(name)
+                            and _strip_the(street).startswith(_strip_the(name))
+                        )
+                    ):
+                        repo_packed_name.append({"gramps_id": rid, "name": name})
+                        break
+            except Exception as exc:  # pylint: disable=broad-except
+                self._errors.record("repositories: address checks", exc, repo)
+                continue
+        out["repos_unused"] = repo_unused
+        out["repos_address_is_name"] = repo_dup_addr
+        out["repos_packed_address"] = repo_packed_name
+        return out
+
+    def collect_db_stats(self, db: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        """Scan repositories, sources, citations, notes, people and media."""
+        self._errors = _ScanErrors()
+
+        def _safe_list(method_name: str) -> list[Any]:
+            try:
+                return list(getattr(db, method_name)())
+            except Exception as exc:  # pylint: disable=broad-except
+                self._errors.record("database iteration (%s)" % method_name, exc, None)
+                return []
+                return []
+
+        people = _safe_list("iter_people")
+        sources = _safe_list("iter_sources")
+        citations = _safe_list("iter_citations")
+        repos = _safe_list("iter_repositories")
+        notes = _safe_list("iter_notes")
+        media_objs = _safe_list("iter_media")
+        events = _safe_list("iter_events")
+
+        stats: dict[str, Any] = {
+            "people": len(people),
+            "sources": len(sources),
+            "repositories": len(repos),
+            "citations": len(citations),
+            "notes": len(notes),
+            "media": len(media_objs),
+        }
+
+        # Citations ----------------------------------------------------
+        cites_by_source: Counter = Counter()
+        no_page = 0
+        with_media = 0
+        for cit in citations:
+            try:
+                src_handle = cit.get_reference_handle()
+                if src_handle:
+                    cites_by_source[str(src_handle)] += 1
+                if not (cit.get_page() or "").strip():
+                    no_page += 1
+                if cit.get_media_list():
+                    with_media += 1
+            except Exception as exc:  # pylint: disable=broad-except
+                self._errors.record(
+                    "citations: source link/page/media counts", exc, cit
+                )
+                continue
+        stats["citations_no_page"] = no_page
+        stats["citations_with_media"] = with_media
+
+        # Sources ------------------------------------------------------
+        conflated_sources = []
+        source_rows = []
+        norm_groups: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = defaultdict(list)
+        tree_handles = set()
+        for src in sources:
+            title = str(src.get_title() or "")
+            handle = str(src.get_handle() or "")
+            row = {
+                "title": title,
+                "gramps_id": str(src.get_gramps_id() or ""),
+                "handle": handle,
+                "repo_count": len(list(src.get_reporef_list())),
+                "citations": cites_by_source.get(handle, 0),
+            }
+            source_rows.append(row)
+            if is_tree_source_title(title):
+                tree_handles.add(handle)
+            elements = detect_title_elements(title)
+            if len(elements) >= 2:
+                conflated_sources.append(dict(row, elements_detected=elements))
+            key = normalize_source_title(title)
+            if key:
+                norm_groups[key].append(row)
+
+        stats["source_rows"] = source_rows
+        stats["conflated_sources"] = conflated_sources
+        stats["sources_no_repo"] = [r for r in source_rows if r["repo_count"] == 0]
+        stats["near_duplicates"] = [g for g in norm_groups.values() if len(g) > 1]
+        stats["tree_citations"] = sum(cites_by_source[h] for h in tree_handles)
+        tree_high = 0
+        for cit in citations:
+            try:
+                if (
+                    str(cit.get_reference_handle()) in tree_handles
+                    and int(cit.get_confidence_level()) >= 3
+                ):
+                    tree_high += 1
+            except Exception as exc:  # pylint: disable=broad-except
+                self._errors.record("citations: confidence level", exc, cit)
+                continue
+        stats["tree_conf_high"] = tree_high
+
+        # Repositories -------------------------------------------------
+        stats["repo_rows"] = [
+            {
+                "name": str(repo.get_name() or ""),
+                "gramps_id": str(repo.get_gramps_id() or ""),
+                "handle": str(repo.get_handle() or ""),
+            }
+            for repo in repos
+        ]
+
+        # Placement / hygiene checks (read-only) ------------------------
+        try:
+            stats.update(
+                self.collect_placement_stats(
+                    sources,
+                    citations,
+                    repos,
+                    cites_by_source,
+                    stats["near_duplicates"],
+                )
+            )
+        except Exception as exc:  # pylint: disable=broad-except
+            self._errors.record("new placement checks (all skipped)", exc, None)
+
+        # People -------------------------------------------------------
+        stats["people_unsourced"] = sum(
+            1
+            for person in people
+            if not self._person_has_citation(person, db, self._errors)
+        )
+
+        # Notes --------------------------------------------------------
+        debris = []
+        long_notes = []
+        for note in notes:
+            try:
+                text = self._note_text(note).strip()
+                preview = " ".join(text.split())[:80]
+                gid = str(note.get_gramps_id() or "")
+                if is_debris_text(text):
+                    debris.append({"gramps_id": gid, "preview": preview})
+                elif len(text) >= LONG_NOTE_CHARS:
+                    long_notes.append(
+                        {"gramps_id": gid, "length": len(text), "preview": preview}
+                    )
+            except Exception as exc:  # pylint: disable=broad-except
+                self._errors.record("notes: text scan", exc, note)
+                continue
+        stats["notes_debris"] = debris
+        stats["notes_long"] = long_notes
+
+        # Media --------------------------------------------------------
+        absolute = 0
+        basenames: Counter = Counter()
+        for media in media_objs:
+            try:
+                path = str(media.get_path() or "")
+                if os.path.isabs(path) or path[1:3] in (":\\", ":/"):
+                    absolute += 1
+                basenames[os.path.basename(path.replace("\\", "/")).lower()] += 1
+            except Exception as exc:  # pylint: disable=broad-except
+                self._errors.record("media: path scan", exc, media)
+                continue
+        stats["media_absolute_count"] = absolute
+        stats["media_dup_basenames"] = {
+            base: count for base, count in basenames.items() if base and count > 1
+        }
+
+        # Events -------------------------------------------------------
+        custom = 0
+        for event in events:
+            try:
+                if event.get_type().is_custom():
+                    custom += 1
+            except Exception as exc:  # pylint: disable=broad-except
+                self._errors.record("events: custom type scan", exc, event)
+                continue
+        stats["custom_events_total"] = custom
+        stats["scan_errors"] = self._errors.as_list()
+        return stats
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _format_scan_errors(stats: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
+        """Report which Gramps calls failed, so a low count is not mistaken for
+        a clean database."""
+        errors = stats.get("scan_errors", [])
+        if not errors:
+            return ["Scan health: every check completed without errors.", ""]
+        total = sum(e["count"] for e in errors)
+        lines = [
+            "Scan health: %d error(s) in %d place(s). Counts below for the "
+            "affected steps may be incomplete." % (total, len(errors))
+        ]
+        for err in errors[:10]:
+            lines.append(
+                "- %s: %dx %s in %s(): %s%s"
+                % (
+                    err["where"],
+                    err["count"],
+                    err["error_type"],
+                    err["function"],
+                    err["message"] or "(no message)",
+                    " [first seen on %s]" % err["example"] if err["example"] else "",
+                )
+            )
+        if len(errors) > 10:
+            lines.append("- ... and %d more (see the Gramps log)." % (len(errors) - 10))
+        lines.append("")
+        return lines
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _format_placement(stats: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
+        """Report lines for the placement / hygiene checks."""
+        get = stats.get
+        out: list[str] = []
+
+        # Citation text in the wrong place
+        frag = get("page_fragments", [])
+        frag_total = sum(n for _, n in frag)
+        if frag_total:
+            out.append(
+                "- Citation pages that start mid-sentence (text cut from the "
+                "source title): %d." % frag_total
+            )
+            for label, n in frag[:3]:
+                out.append("  ↳ %d on %s" % (n, label))
+        if get("page_access_dates"):
+            out.append(
+                "- Access dates typed into the page field: %d (%d of them have an "
+                "empty citation Date)."
+                % (get("page_access_dates", 0), get("page_access_dates_no_date", 0))
+            )
+        templates = get("page_templates", [])
+        if templates and get("citations_no_page", 0) < get("citations", 0):
+            out.append(
+                "- Page text is repetitive: %d distinct values; most common patterns:"
+                % get("page_distinct", 0)
+            )
+            for tmpl, n in templates[:3]:
+                out.append("  ↳ %dx %s" % (n, tmpl[:90]))
+        like_src = get("page_source_like", {})
+        if like_src:
+            out.append(
+                "- Citation pages that read like a collection name (belongs in "
+                "the source title?): %d sources affected." % len(like_src)
+            )
+            for label, pages in list(like_src.items())[:4]:
+                out.append("  ↳ %s: %s" % (label, "; ".join(pages[:2])[:100]))
+        if get("citations_empty"):
+            out.append(
+                "- Completely empty citations (no page, date, attribute, note or "
+                "media): %d of %d." % (get("citations_empty", 0), get("citations", 0))
+            )
+            for label, n in get("citations_empty_by_source", [])[:3]:
+                out.append("  ↳ %d on %s" % (n, label))
+
+        # Source field hygiene
+        bad = get("sources_bad_fields", [])
+        if bad:
+            out.append(
+                "- Sources with markup, stray quotes or stray whitespace in a "
+                "field: %d." % len(bad)
+            )
+            for row in bad[:4]:
+                detail = "; ".join(
+                    "%s (%s)" % (f, ", ".join(p)) for f, p in row["problems"].items()
+                )
+                out.append(
+                    "  ↳ %s '%s': %s" % (row["gramps_id"], row["title"][:50], detail)
+                )
+        cstyle = get("sources_citation_style", [])
+        if cstyle:
+            out.append(
+                "- Source titles that look like a pasted citation string: %d."
+                % len(cstyle)
+            )
+            for row in cstyle[:3]:
+                out.append(
+                    "  ↳ %s '%s' (%d citations)"
+                    % (row["gramps_id"], row["title"][:60], row["citations"])
+                )
+        non_titles = get("sources_non_titles", [])
+        if non_titles:
+            out.append(
+                "- Source titles that are really a URL, domain or filename: %d."
+                % len(non_titles)
+            )
+            for row in non_titles[:4]:
+                out.append(
+                    "  ↳ %s '%s' (%s)" % (row["gramps_id"], row["title"], row["kind"])
+                )
+        placeholders = get("sources_placeholder", [])
+        if placeholders:
+            cites = sum(r["citations"] for r in placeholders)
+            out.append(
+                "- Placeholder sources ('Unknown' / blank): %d, holding %d citations."
+                % (len(placeholders), cites)
+            )
+        unused = get("sources_unused", [])
+        if unused:
+            out.append("- Sources with no citations at all: %d." % len(unused))
+
+        # Duplicates the strict title match misses
+        loose = get("dupes_loose", [])
+        if loose:
+            out.append(
+                "- Duplicate sources hidden by 'U.S.' / punctuation differences "
+                "(safe to merge): %d clusters." % len(loose)
+            )
+            for group in loose[:5]:
+                out.append(
+                    "  ↳ "
+                    + "; ".join(
+                        "%s '%s'" % (r["gramps_id"], r["title"][:45]) for r in group[:3]
+                    )
+                )
+        variants = get("dupes_year_variants", [])
+        if variants:
+            out.append(
+                "- Same collection, different year range (check before merging): "
+                "%d clusters." % len(variants)
+            )
+            for group in variants[:4]:
+                out.append(
+                    "  ↳ "
+                    + "; ".join(
+                        "%s '%s'" % (r["gramps_id"], r["title"][:45]) for r in group[:3]
+                    )
+                )
+
+        # Repository hygiene
+        r_unused = get("repos_unused")
+        if r_unused and hasattr(r_unused, "__len__"):
+            out.append("- Repositories not linked to any source: %d." % len(r_unused))
+        r_addr_name = get("repos_address_is_name")
+        if r_addr_name and hasattr(r_addr_name, "__len__"):
+            out.append(
+                "- Repositories whose address just repeats the name: %d."
+                % len(r_addr_name)
+            )
+        r_packed = get("repos_packed_address")
+        if r_packed and hasattr(r_packed, "__len__"):
+            out.append(
+                "- Repositories with a long address field (likely several "
+                "places or notes packed in): %d." % len(r_packed)
+            )
+        return out

+    def format_analysis(self, stats: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
+        """Formats the collected statistics dictionary into a deep, descriptive report body."""
+        get = stats.get
+        lines = []
+
+        # 1. Database Totals Block
+        lines.append(
+            "Database totals: %d people, %d sources, %d repositories, %d citations, %d notes, %d media."
+            % (
+                get("people", 0),
+                get("sources", 0),
+                get("repositories", 0),
+                get("citations", 0),
+                get("notes", 0),
+                get("media", 0),
+            )
+        )
+        lines.append("")
+
+        # 1b. Scan health: Gramps methods that raised exceptions
+        lines.extend(self._format_scan_errors(stats))
+
+        # 2. Positive Alignments / Best Practices
+        lines.append("Where it matches best practice:")
+        lines.append(
+            "- Most sources are collection-level with specifics in citations (Evidence Explained approach)."
+        )
+        lines.append("")
+
+        # 3. Deficiencies / Diagnostic Room for Improvement
+        lines.append("Where it falls short:")
+
+        # Repository Missing Log
+        lines.append(
+            "- Sources without a repository link: %d of %d."
+            % (len(get("sources_no_repo", [])), get("sources", 0))
+        )
+
+        # Conflated Smashed Fields Log
+        conflated = get("conflated_sources", [])
+        lines.append(
+            "- Conflated Fields: %d sources contain mixed data types crammed together."
+            % len(conflated)
+        )
+        for row in conflated[:10]:
+            lines.append(
+                "  * %s: '%s'\n    ↳ Found elements: %s"
+                % (
+                    row.get("gramps_id"),
+                    row.get("title"),
+                    ", ".join(row.get("elements_detected", [])),
+                )
+            )
+
+        # Citation Pinpoint Page Tracking
+        lines.append(
+            "- Citations with no pinpoint Volume/Page detail: %d of %d."
+            % (get("citations_no_page", 0), get("citations", 0))
+        )
+
+        # FamilySearch Tree Downgrade Metrics
+        if get("tree_citations"):
+            lines.append(
+                "- Collaborative Tree citations found: %d (Rated High/Very High confidence: %d)."
+                % (get("tree_citations", 0), get("tree_conf_high", 0))
+            )
+
+        # Unsourced Individuals Check
+        lines.append(
+            "- Individuals with zero attached source citations: %d of %d."
+            % (get("people_unsourced", 0), get("people", 0))
+        )
+
+        # Near-Duplicate String Groups Match
+        dupes = get("near_duplicates", [])
+        lines.append("- Near-duplicate source title clusters found: %d." % len(dupes))
+        for group in dupes[:7]:
+            joined = "; ".join(
+                "%s '%s'" % (r.get("gramps_id"), r.get("title")) for r in group[:4]
+            )
+            lines.append("  ↳ Cluster match: " + joined)
+
+        # Extra placement & hygiene findings ----------------------------
+        lines.extend(self._format_placement(stats))
+
+        # Automated Export Junk Log
+        debris = get("notes_debris", [])
+        lines.append(
+            "- Import debris & migration logs hiding inside notes: %d rows."
+            % len(debris)
+        )
+        for row in debris[:5]:
+            lines.append(
+                "  ↳ Note %s preview: %s" % (row.get("gramps_id"), row.get("preview"))
+            )
+
+        # Long Sketched Blocks Counter
+        long_notes = get("notes_long", [])
+        if long_notes:
+            lines.append("- Long life-sketch narrative notes:")
+            for row in long_notes[:3]:
+                lines.append(
+                    "  ↳ Note %s (%d chars): %s..."
+                    % (row.get("gramps_id"), row.get("length"), row.get("preview"))
+                )
+
+        # Media absolute layout warnings
+        abs_count = get("media_absolute_count", 0)
+        lines.append(
+            "- Media objects carrying absolute hardcoded file paths: %d (Citations with attached media: %d)."
+            % (abs_count, get("citations_with_media", 0))
+        )
+
+        # Duplicate filename warning blocks
+        dup_media = get("media_dup_basenames", {})
+        if dup_media:
+            lines.append(
+                "- Duplicate filenames imported multiple times across different records:"
+            )
+            for base, count in list(dup_media.items())[:5]:
+                lines.append("  * %s (Imported %dx)" % (base, count))
+
+        # Leftover layout warning flags
+        if get("custom_events_total"):
+            lines.append(
+                "- Custom unsupported unaligned legacy event definitions: %d tags."
+                % get("custom_events_total", 0)
+            )
+
+        lines.append("")
+
+        # 4. Roadmap Step Breakdown Timeline
+        lines.append("Suggested order of fixes:")
+        lines.append(
+            "1. Run 'Unpack Conflated Source' to isolate hidden repository text strings."
+        )
+        lines.append(
+            "2. Run 'Repository Consolidate' to deduplicate matching repository targets."
+        )
+        lines.append(
+            "3. Run 'Fix Sources' to safely group matching census & collection lines together."
+        )
+        lines.append(
+            "4. Run 'Unpack Conflated Citation' to separate access dates, URLs, and volume/page strings."
+        )
+        lines.append(
+            "5. Run 'Fix Citations' to auto-downgrade online user tree confidence metrics."
+        )
+        lines.append(
+            "6. Run 'Fix Notes' to permanently scrub legacy automated migration log files."
+        )
+        step = 7
+        if (
+            get("sources_bad_fields")
+            or get("sources_citation_style")
+            or get("page_fragments")
+            or get("page_access_dates_no_date")
+        ):
+            lines.append(
+                "%d. Clean source titles (markup, quotes) and move access dates and "
+                "entry detail out of the source and into the citation." % step
+            )
+            step += 1
+        if get("page_source_like") or get("sources_non_titles"):
+            lines.append(
+                "%d. Review the flagged pages and URL/filename titles by hand; "
+                "there are usually only a handful." % step
+            )
+            step += 1
+        if get("sources_placeholder"):
+            lines.append(
+                "%d. Merge or delete the placeholder 'Unknown' sources." % step
+            )
+
+        return "\n".join(lines)
+

+def collect_db_stats(db: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Module-level convenience wrapper used by the fix dialogs."""
+    return GWizardCitationReport().collect_db_stats(db)

+#
+# Field detectors (single copy, used by the report and the repair engine)
+#

+FIELD_REPO_PATTERNS = re.compile(
+    r"https?://|www\.|familysearch|ancestry|newspapers\.com|find\s?a\s?grave"
+    r"|myheritage|legacy\.com",
+    re.IGNORECASE,
+)
+FIELD_SOURCE_PATTERNS = re.compile(
+    r"census|death\s+certificate|birth\s+record|marriage\s+index|vital\s+records"
+    r"|church\s+records|obituary\s+index",
+    re.IGNORECASE,
+)
+FIELD_CITATION_PATTERNS = re.compile(
+    r"page\s+\d+|vol(ume)?\s+\d+|cert(ificate)?\s+\d+|accessed\s+\d+|entry\s+for"
+    r"|household\s+\d+|line\s+\d+|memorial\s+id",
+    re.IGNORECASE,
+)
